Medzhybizh Old Jewish Cemetery

Jewish Cemetery · Khmelnytska oblast, Ukraine

Not demolished. Medzhybizh holds one of the most significant sites in this entire collection: the Baal Shem Tov, founder of Hasidism, resided here from 1740 to 1760, and his grave remains a popular pilgrimage destination in Hasidic circles to this day. Jews are first mentioned in the region in the early 16th century, with an organized community by 1511; a Jewish cemetery was laid out in 1570, alongside 70 Jewish householders, and by the early 17th century Medzhybizh had become one of the largest Jewish communities in Podolia. The community suffered during the Khmelnytsky massacre of 1650 and again in the early 18th century, but rebuilt, reaching a peak of about 6,040 people (73 percent) by 1897, supporting nine synagogues by 1914. A pogrom in 1919, staged by forces of the Directory, killed all the Jews remaining in the city at that time. During WWII, a ghetto established in autumn 1941 saw 1,000 prisoners executed on September 22, 1942; many others died of hunger and typhoid that winter, though several Jews were saved by Ukrainian peasants. This is the older of Medzhybizh's two Jewish cemeteries, existing by the mid-16th century based on its preserved tombstones.
